solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Don’t look at topless foreign rogue (6)

indicatorNotes.topless: a topless word has lost its first letter
indicatorNotes.rogue: letters gone rogue have strayed out of order

blocks.note: FOREIGN without its top letter F

annotation.surface: A warning to avert your eyes from some shady foreign scoundrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foreign rogue' reads as a person, but 'rogue' is an instruction and 'foreign' only supplies letters once decapitated.
annotation.definitionFit: To ignore something is deliberately not to look at it or heed it.

entries.clue: Swimmer’s clobber is rubbish (10)

blocks.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer; with the possessive 'S
to clobber someone is to wallop them

annotation.surface: Someone sneers at a swimmer's gear as tatty junk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes or gear, which suits the swimmer, but here it is the verb 'hit hard'. CODSWALLOP is British slang for nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Codswallop means nonsense, rubbish talk.

entries.clue: Cycling surfaces with dark material for VIP (4)

indicatorNotes.Cycling: the letters go round like a wheel, the last one coming to the front

blocks.note: to tar a road is to surface it with black tar

annotation.surface: Roads are being blacktopped for a cycle race, to welcome a celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' pretends to be about bikes on newly tarred roads; it actually tells you to rotate the letters of TARS.
annotation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrity, a very important person.

entries.clue: Egotistical person starts to splash everyone in stream (6)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the next two words
indicatorNotes.in: those letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: a stream = to pour, as rain does
first letters of Splash and Everyone

annotation.surface: A show-off at the pool splashes everybody in the water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stream' is a verb here, to pour, not a brook; 'splash everyone in stream' paints bathers, which hides the instruction to put letters inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A poseur puts on airs to impress, a self-regarding person.

entries.clue: Extremely trendy black suit (2,6)

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable
spades is one of the two black suits in cards

annotation.surface: A very fashionable black outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'suit' as clothing and 'extremely' as an intensifier on 'trendy'; both belong to other jobs.
annotation.definitionFit: Having something in spades means having it in abundance, to an extreme degree.

entries.clue: Upset father managed to put on calm air (10)

indicatorNotes.Upset: in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down
indicatorNotes.to put on: calm puts on RAN like a garment, wrapping around it

blocks.note: pa = father, turned upside down in this down clue
peace = calm, the outer piece
ran a business = managed it; this goes inside PEACE

annotation.surface: An agitated dad has to fake composure.
annotation.walkthrough: AP, then PEACE wearing RAN: PEA(RAN)CE. The surface makes 'calm air' a single phrase, but 'air' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An air is the look or manner someone presents, their appearance.

entries.clue: Insect fine climbing in bit of foliage (4)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue the F climbs from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: a leaf is one piece of foliage; its last letter is F, the usual abbreviation for fine
F, the pencil-grade abbreviation; it is the F already at the foot of LEAF, and it is this letter that moves up

annotation.surface: A healthy insect crawling up through a leaf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is the usual abbreviation F, already sitting at the foot of LEAF; move it up and you have the insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the flea is the classic jumping, biting insect.

entries.clue: Manner of speaking is standard way around Charlie (8)

indicatorNotes.around: to go around something is to encircle it, so LANE encircles C

blocks.note: par is the standard score
a lane is a way
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A style of speech described as the normal route round someone called Charlie.
annotation.walkthrough: PAR, then LAN(C)E.
annotation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking, as in 'legal parlance'.

entries.clue: There are no people in this brown dress, according to Spooner (5,4)

annotation.definition: There are no people in this

indicatorNotes.according to Spooner: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: to toast bread is to brown it; this word gives up its T sound and takes the G
a gown is a dress; it hands over its G and collects the T

annotation.surface: A brown frock so dull that nobody is wearing it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a colour, but it is the verb: toasting browns bread.
annotation.definitionFit: A ghost town is a deserted settlement, empty of people.

entries.clue: Dance crew performing out of abandoned workplace (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: CREW is taken out of WORKPLACE
indicatorNotes.abandoned: the remaining letters are let loose, free to rearrange

blocks.note: WORKPLACE with the letters of CREW (C, R, E, W) taken out
a working crew; the word CREW supplies the letters removed from WORKPLACE

annotation.surface: A work gang dances as they leave a derelict factory.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters of CREW are scattered through WORKPLACE rather than in a row, so they are removed one by one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the polka is one particular Bohemian dance in quick two-time.

entries.clue: Watch old boy start tennis match (7)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
each tennis point starts with a serve

annotation.surface: Look on as an elderly man opens a tennis game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a noun or an order to the old boy; it is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to observe something is to watch it closely, as a birdwatcher observes.

entries.clue: State border guards backing rule (7)

indicatorNotes.guards: LIP guards AVER by surrounding it
indicatorNotes.backing: the whole thing then runs backwards

blocks.note: a lip is an edge or border, the outer piece
to aver is to state firmly; it sits inside LIP

annotation.surface: A nation's frontier troops support the regime.
annotation.walkthrough: LI(AVER)P, read backwards. 'State' looks like a country and 'border guards' like soldiers; in fact 'guards' is the verb that wraps one piece round the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of holding sway: a view that prevails rules the day.

entries.clue: Charmed with change of demeanour (9)

indicatorNotes.change of: the letters of the next word are changed around

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is delighted by another's new attitude.
annotation.walkthrough: The British spelling with OU is what makes this anagram work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone enamoured is taken with, charmed by, another.

entries.clue: Bit drunk leaving celebration in stupidly big boat (5,5)

indicatorNotes.drunk: BIT staggers: its letters are not together in CELEBRATION
indicatorNotes.leaving: to leave a place is to go out of it, so BIT's letters go out of CELEBRATION
indicatorNotes.stupidly: the rest, plus IN, is rearranged

blocks.note: CELEBRATION with B, I and T removed; they are scattered, not in a row
the word itself, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Partygoers, a little tipsy, wander off a huge cruise ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit drunk' reads as 'slightly tipsy'; in fact BIT is the thing removed, with 'drunk' saying its letters are scattered.
annotation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship.

entries.clue: Reviewed some fines irritatingly increased (5)

indicatorNotes.Reviewed: read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.some: only part of the following words

blocks.note: fiNES IRritatingly, the run of letters straddling the two words

annotation.surface: Penalties have been reassessed and annoyingly gone up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Reviewed' and 'increased' both about fines; only 'increased' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Same part of speech: a price that has risen has gone up, increased.

entries.clue: Rate water sources for plants (10)

blocks.note: a rate of travel is a speed
wells supply water

annotation.surface: Assessing irrigation supplies for a garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like a verb, 'assess', but it is the noun SPEED.
annotation.definitionFit: Speedwells are low plants with small blue flowers.

entries.clue: Take up little room after turning in bed (7)

indicatorNotes.after turning: the word is turned round first
indicatorNotes.in: 'in bed' means lying inside the bed, so the turned word goes within COT

blocks.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison; it is turned round
a cot is a small bed, the outer piece

annotation.surface: A restless sleeper tossing in bed barely takes up any space.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take up little room' is a complete phrase on the surface, a sleeper curled small; split it after 'Take up' to find the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To take up is to gather or collect, as a collection is taken up.

entries.clue: Rain-cloud at sea overlooking one large vessel (8)

blocks.note: the words themselves
one = I, left out
RANCLOUD rearranged

annotation.surface: A storm cloud over the ocean looms above a big ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large vessel' paints a ship to go with the sea; it is a big cooking pot.
annotation.definitionFit: Misdirection by sense: 'vessel' suggests a ship at sea, but a cauldron is a vessel in the pot sense, a large one for boiling.

entries.clue: Ride conveyance to marsh with horse going north (8)

indicatorNotes.going north: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards

blocks.note: the word itself
a bog is a marsh
a nag is a horse; NAG upwards

annotation.surface: Instructions for riding a horse to a marsh up north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ride conveyance' is an odd pairing that hides the definition: something you ride on, a sled.
annotation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sled ridden downhill over snow.

entries.clue: True friends in ceremonial clothes (7)

indicatorNotes.clothes: the words clothe the answer, wrapped round it

blocks.note: friendS IN CEREmonial

annotation.surface: Loyal companions dressed in their ceremonial robes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' is a verb here: the phrase 'friends in ceremonial' clothes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a true friend is a sincere one, genuine rather than false.

entries.clue: French article long, abridged for release (5)

blocks.note: un is French for 'a'
PINE (to long) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A lengthy French piece is cut down before publication.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the article; it is the verb 'pine'.
annotation.definitionFit: To unpin something is to release it by taking out the pin.

entries.clue: Service industry employee receiving tip in exchange (9)

blocks.note: barter is trade by exchange
the tip of something is its end; it goes inside BARTER

annotation.surface: A waiter takes a gratuity in return for good service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' fits the service-industry picture as a gratuity; it means the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks, a worker in the hospitality trade.

entries.clue: Rook likely eviscerated other bird (6)

indicatorNotes.eviscerated: gutted: the middle letters are removed

blocks.note: R = rook in chess notation
apt to = likely to
OTHER with its insides (THE) removed

annotation.surface: A rook has probably gutted a different bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rook' is a bird in the surface, which pulls toward it being the definition; it is the chess piece, R.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: raptors are birds of prey such as hawks and eagles, so 'bird' is the wider category.

entries.clue: Cut beetroot quiche in regular parts (6)

blocks.note: beetroot is the colour of deep red
qUiChE, every second letter

annotation.surface: Slicing a beetroot quiche into equal portions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the kitchen instruction; it is the definition, and 'beetroot' is a colour.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the business sense: to cut prices is to reduce them.

entries.clue: Seeing bears run moving quickly (7)

blocks.note: seeing someone = dating them
R = run, as in cricket scores; it goes inside DATING

annotation.surface: Someone spots bears and runs off fast.
annotation.walkthrough: DA(R)TING. 'Bears' looks like animals; it is a verb, 'carries'.
annotation.definitionFit: Darting means moving swiftly and suddenly.

entries.clue: Power to avoid fast attack (4)

indicatorNotes.to avoid: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so P stays out of the word

blocks.note: fast = RAPID; P is the physics symbol for power, and it is left out

annotation.surface: Using strength to dodge a swift assault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast attack' reads as one phrase; 'fast' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a raid is one kind of attack, sudden and short.

entries.clue: Herald left Spain and heads for New Delhi (7)

indicatorNotes.heads for: the heads, first letters, of the next words

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
E is Spain's international vehicle code
first letters of New Delhi

annotation.surface: A messenger quits Spain and makes for India's capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Herald' looks like a person; it is the verb, to foretell.
annotation.definitionFit: To portend is to herald, to be a sign of something coming.

entries.clue: Having advanced to the south, go off course (4)

indicatorNotes.to the south: in a down clue, below means after

blocks.note: food that goes off rots
A = advanced, as in A level

annotation.surface: A traveller who pushed on south has strayed from the route.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go off course' reads as one phrase meaning stray; split it, and 'course' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A rota is a course or round of duties taken in turn.

entries.clue: Fruit son peeled, flipping bad (5)

indicatorNotes.peeled: the outside letters are stripped off

blocks.note: SON without its outer letters
bad = EVIL, backwards

annotation.surface: A boy peels some fruit that turns out to be rotten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peeled' belongs to the fruit in the surface but acts on 'son'; 'flipping' is also mild British slang for 'damned'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the olive is one fruit among many, the stone fruit of the olive tree.

entries.clue: Preacher’s source of antagonistic mail law enforcers uncovered (9)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective: belonging to an apostle, the model preacher

indicatorNotes.source of: the source of a river is where it starts, so the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Antagonistic
mail = post
POLICE without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A minister receives hate mail and the police find out where it came from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' suggests the police exposing the source; it tells you to strip POLICE of its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Apostolic means of the apostles, the first Christian preachers.
